3. x1781-1865, 19 cells: 但右同斷ニ付別段差渡候役員宛行之分如斯 — annotates item 2.
4. x1666-1734: 〃同拾四石 = 14 koku rice.
5. x1526-1600: 〃錢七百六拾八貫文 = 768 kanmon. 七 (not 九) confirmed at 2.6x.
6. x1369-1464, 28 cells: 但和漂民護送使上士壹人上下四人卒族貳人船附壹人大坂長崎之
7. x1253-1328, 10 cells: 間召仕候宛行之分如斯 — items 6+7 are one two-column note annotating BOTH item 4 (rice) and item 5 (cash).
8. x1129-1205: 〃同貳千八百八拾八貫文 = 2,888 kanmon. 千 has the slanted stroke on top (checked against 十 at 2.6x, tV234.png), so this is 2,888 and not 288.
9. x973-1067, 28 cells: 但朝鮮ゟ差渡候漂民駕船護送使乘船且本藩ヨリ大坂長崎之間途
10. x850-926, 11 cells: 還之節借入候船賃共如斯 — items 9+10 are one two-column note annotating item 8.
11. x728-796: 譯官渡來入費 — a new item heading, indented one character below the amount columns to its left, which is the standard HI layout for a sub-heading followed by its amounts.
12. x582-661: 一米五百貳拾三石八斗貳升五合九才 = 523.82509 koku (descending, 勺 skipped).
13. x454-533: 一錢貳萬六千八百四拾六貫五百四拾四文 = 26,846 kan 544 mon. 六千 (slanted top stroke) checked at 2.6x, tV6.png.

ONE UNCERTAIN GLYPH, stated plainly: cell 10 of column x973-1067 (y2186-2250), between 民 and 船. The type is heavily inked there and the strokes bleed together; I ran three thresholds, an unsharp-masked 14x zoom, and an ASCII pixel dump. What survives is a stroke that sweeps down-left and ends detached at mid-height on the left edge (x992-1000, y2213-2219), a detached round dot at the lower-left (x994-1006, y2234-2246), and a dense body with internal horizontal bars. The lower-left detached dot is the leftmost of 灬 and the mid-height tail is the 丿 of 力, which makes the character 駕 (力+口 over 馬). Reading 漂民駕船 alongside 護送使乘船 gives two vessels — the castaways' vessel and the escort envoy's vessel — which the third clause (hired ship fares) then completes. I could not resolve this glyph to certainty and flag it as my one uncertain reading on the page.

A second, minor one: the small ligature at cell 17 of column x2037-2128 (人夫ゟ) is the same glyph as cell 4 of column x973-1067 (朝鮮ゟ) — I put the two side by side at 6x (gl2.png) and they are identical, so I transcribe both as ゟ. In 朝鮮ゟ it plainly reads より; after 人夫 the sense is dative, so the modern reading I give is 人夫に.

ARITHMETIC NET: this page has no total-and-components group — no 男/女 split, no 人口/人員 total, no 本田/新田 or 内訳 summing to a 合高/草高. The four ditto-marked amounts are separate line items under a heading that stands on the previous page, and the two 一-marked amounts are the rice and cash halves of the 譯官渡來入費 entry (different units, so they do not sum). There is therefore nothing on this page to cross-foot, and I did not invent one.

MASTER: the brief supplied no MASTER rows and no fascicle/table for this page, so there was nothing to cross-check against; every reading above is from the scan.

BOXES: for each of the 15 elements I cropped a generous region, thresholded px<125, projected onto rows and columns, took first..last inked row/col and padded 10px. Minimum horizontal gap between adjacent padded boxes is 14px, so no two rectangles overlap; the header box and the page-number box share x but are 1,270px apart in y. Rendered the overlay once to _final.png and read it: every box is flush around its column, none clips a glyph, none sits on whitespace, and the faint facing-page bleed-through in the lower middle of the sheet (much lighter ink, around x1600-1900) is correctly left unboxed. No second pass was needed.
proposal.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 1 (Izuhara)
proposal.page_topic: Izuhara domain expenditure on Korea relations
proposal.page_summary_en: A continuation page from the fascicle-1 expenditure account of Izuhara domain (Tsushima), carrying no maru-marker and therefore belonging in its entirety to that domain. Four ditto-marked amounts head the page, each followed by an explanatory 但 note: 14.56901 koku of rice for officials dispatched separately; 14 koku of rice together with 768 kan of cash for the mission escorting Japanese castaways, made up of one senior samurai, four attendants, two sotsu-rank men and one ship hand employed between Osaka and Nagasaki; and 2,888 kan of cash for the vessel carrying castaways sent over from Korea, the escort envoy's own vessel, and ship-hire on the outward and return passage between the domain and Osaka and Nagasaki. The left half of the page opens a fresh item, 譯官渡來入費 (expenses for the visits of the Korean interpreter-officials), charged at 523.82509 koku of rice and 26,846 kan 544 mon of cash. The whole sheet documents the fiscal cost to Tsushima of its monopoly role in relations with Korea.
